One time my teacher was pregnant and somebody sent her a box of these cookies and she loved them and she suggested Hope's Cookies to me so I went.  Good story, huh?

The person that helped me was very nice, extremely patient, and didn't mind explaining the pricing to me.  It came to about $10.25 for a dozen in a bag or $13 for the same number of cookies in a box.  I got a little of everything but really enjoyed the triple chocolate the most, but I really like chocolate.  I'd definitely go back, but next time I need help eating a dozen cookies!!

God, why can't I take the train more. 
This by FAR is the biggest hidden gem in the city. 
Take your Mom on a fancy train ride into the sprawling suburbs..just leave 5+ hours for a visit to Bridgewaters.

Overstating it?

i think not. Considering where it is..what you would expect.. this exceeds everything you would imagine. Most bars get by on typical pub food.. (fried this, fried that, bleagh). Or better yet, the striped shirt beer list (Bud, Bud Light, Miller..) you get the picture. NONE OF THIS IS HERE!! Bridgewaters ever-changing beer list is AMBITIOUS, and TOP-NOTCH. This high level of beer variety and quality is only matched by their menu. Delightful, inspiring, this place makes me want to be a better beer drinker. 

Do yourself a favor.. go here.

Chris Kearse, as always, culinary genius. 

They have a special tasting menu once a month, focusing on a specific ingredient. Just in time for fall, we went for the pumpkin tasting menu! Every dish that came out was beautifully plated, tasted delicious, and wasn't redundant in flavors or taste. The tiny restaurant is BYOB, yet wasn't uncomfortably cramped. 

Personally, I loved the appetizer with pumpkin, apple foam (I am pro foam everything), as well as the consumme with mushroom. Quail stuffed with pumpkin stuffing, and kampachi sashimi in a stone bowl with some pumpkin seeds and asian pear, cut out in little stars. 

Would definitely return for future tasting menus, or even a la carte. Continuing the kudos and popular opinion of food coma happiness!

The Picadilly is a must visit place in Maplewood. I used to live about two blocks away so I have been there several times and I have never had anything that wasn't delicious. My most recent visit was last night for Valentines Day. 

I ordered the Cajun pasta. It was absolutely delicious. It had so many great flavors in it. The best part was the fact that it tasted nothing at all like what I expected. I'm glad it didn't because this was way better. 

My fiancée got a filet mignon. It was also delicious. It was cooked perfectly. There's not very many places where you can get an 8oz filet for like $23 either. It came with a baked potato and a salad. She said the poppyseed dressing was great. 

Other things I have had there are the baby back ribs, double cheeseburger, wings, chicken pot pie, and I'm sure there are more but I am forgetting at this moment. The ribs are some of the best ribs I've ever had - I've had quite a few in my life. The chicken pot pie is huge and has an amazing flakey crust. The wings are the burgers are great and should not be dismissed if that's more of the mood you are in. 

Next visit: pulled pork stuffed barbecue ravioli. I can't wait!

This is not a review about a restaurant. This is a story about a dining experience. One that I have enjoyed for many years and one that occurs 363 days a year from 5pm-10pm and until 11pm on Fridays and Saturdays.  But don't worry; Bern's does not close if diners are seated. And veteran server Drew will be there until 7am the next morning in case your dessert takes longer than anticipated. 

Bern's was created through decades of hardwork, passion, and commitment. Bern and his wife Gert had a vision for a restaurant that had good food, good service, and even better customers. 

From the moment you pull your car into the valet at Bern's you know you're in for a special night. Everybody is dressed up and as you enter this large white building that seems very mysterious from the outside, you open the doors and will be amazed by the red velvet walls, the professionalism and ambiance of this restaurant. 

The food is unbelievable! Bern's only buys three primal cuts, steaks are dry aged for six weeks, and the steaks are only cut once you order them. You can chose from 60 different cuts, thicknesses, and weight. Each individual steak has 32 variations in color, juiciness and cooking time that it can be ordered. For every ounce of fat that's cut off your steak an additional ounce of meat is added so a 10oz steak IS a 10oz steak. They also serve lamb, fresh fish brought in daily, and a delicious Chicken Gert (original recipe courtesy of Gert's mother, Rose). They can also list up to 10 allergies, sensitivities and dietary needs for your order.

The ice cubes are filtered, that should be enough for you to go right now!

The wine... This can be its own review. Bern's has the world's largest privately owned wine collection. With more than half a million wines with 6,500 different labels, there is no shortage of wine at Bern's. Their wine cellar is kept at 50 degrees and their wine list is 185 pages, in it's 65th edition. There are 150 wines served by the glass, and the on staff sommeliers can answer any question you have about their wine. 

The service, is unlike any others. Servers train up to two years before they can even serve on the main dining room floor. That's longer than most people even serve at a typical restaurant. They go through the ranks first wearing a maroon, then silver, and if you're ever worthy enough a gold tie. There is a "black jacket exam" (before servers graduated from red to black jackets) that they must pass in order to serve in the main dining floor.  Servers work on the farm, in the kitchen, in the dessert room, and know every facet of the restaurant as Bern's did while creating this gem. 

The dessert room upstairs, formally named the Harry Waugh Dessert Room has chocolate imported from France. The desserts are masterpieces, created by executive pastry Chef Kim. The room took seven years to build and was finally completed in 1985. Old wine cask staves were turned into booths, and Bern's had a vision for this dessert room to be a place to unwind and relax after dinner. It's intimate setting and adjustable music makes it perfect for any occasion. If you didn't make it to dinner, you can head over to Bern's and eat dessert, and experience just one part of what this dining experience has to offer. 

The thing I truly like most about Bern's is the people. My three favorite people at Bern's and the people I must see when I visit are Frank, Drew, and Chef Hab. Frank is always at the front desk greeting his customers, piloting the floor, and making sure everyone is satisfied. Drew is the best server I have ever had and a very good happy and humble person that makes my night at Bern's so much better.  Chef Hab is in the back cooking up the steaks and running the kitchen. But more importantly they've become my friends! This place is really part of my family! They have been there during so many special occasions, such as a birthday, graduation or anniversary. I find myself creating celebrations just to go to Bern's and I know it will be great because of people like Frank, Drew and Chef Hab.

Every aspect of this restaurant has a story and everything in this restaurant displays the passion and perfectionist personality that Bern's grew up with. It's the curiosity for perfection, the thirst for knowledge, and the requirement of excellence. It's the reason why David (current owner and son of Bern's) and Christina (David's wife) have been able to make Bern's prosper and expand throughout the last several decades. Passion is not something you can learn or teach, it's something you're born with and it's what makes some people in this world different than others. Passion is what makes Bern's a once in a lifetime dining experience and my passion for Bern's is the reason I took the time to write this story and explain to you that the "Bern's Way" is the right way!

Perfect timing to be able to try a new lunch spot, while the dogs are getting evaluated at a new boarding/grooming place.

Arrived starving! The building is very open and spacious.

We noticed a few tables with pizza, but I had my heart set in the bang bang shrimp.

The server brought  out home baked bread and butter.

I do enjoy bread and especially liked the baguette.

Decided to also try the Blta..

The bang bang shrimp was very satisfying, and plentiful.

Blta was also nicely toasted with thick bread and perfectly cooked French fries.

Glad we stopped, and definitely be back to try the dinner menu.

This is a little suburban Chinese place with a lot of heart. In California where I live I could not give it five stars but here I am glad to find it. The fried wontons with the orange sauce are quite delicious. Surprisingly so. The potstickers are clearly hand rolled. The hot and sour soup has a savory base that I really enjoyed. The double pan fried noodle was tasty with fresh vegetables and beef in a savory sauce.

Frida bakery has mixed reviews from my friend. I like to find out myself for my own experience. The bakery serve lunch and breakfast. The breakfast included many item with bacon. The lunch also good. When I was there, many come in for the soup, I did not try that. 

I got to pieces of their dessert for the my late snack. I have cassada torte and the carrot cake. The cassada torte has a cannoli place on top. The middle has two layers of cake and mousse and a layer of chocolate. The cake is moist and has syrup in it. It is tasty. 

The carrot cake is good. It is top with carrot icing. Layer with cake cream. My experience here is good. No big wow factor. They have outside seating good for the current weather. I was serve quickly. Seem like the customers who eat there enjoy it.

This year, I convinced my dad that we should have real BBQ for our Fourth of July dinner instead of the usual dry, flavorless grilled hamburgers and chicken.  (Don't tell him I said that!)  Having done my research on Yelp, I suggested Russell's, since everyone seemed to rave about it.  Afraid that it might either not be open on the 4th or might sell out, my dad and I headed over yesterday morning (July 3) to check it out.

Expecting that he sells his meat by weight, my dad asked Russell how much he charges per pound.  After greeting us warmly, Russell smiled and said, "I don't sell by the pound--I'm lazy.  How many people do you want to feed?" My dad told him four, and Russell said he'd hook us up.  He asked us what we wanted, and we decided on the pulled pork (a must at any BBQ place!), (pork) ribs, and BBQ chicken. We also got some mac and cheese and sweet potatoes to go with it.  Russell gave us enough food for two meals (see photos), packaged it all up, and explained to us how to reheat it (set in pan of water in oven at 275 for 30-40 min.) I mentioned that it was our first time, and he cut us a deal for $50, which was about $10 less than my dad was expecting to pay.

Other reviews aside, I knew just from smelling the food on the way home that it was going to be amazing--it took a lot of willpower not to sample it, but I was able to resist temptation.  When it came out of the oven tonight, I took some of everything.  Man, oh, man, talk about smoked goodness!  It was the best BBQ I've ever had, beating the pants off of my favorite BBQ establishments in PGH and even Daddy D'z in Atlanta. The pork was so tender, moist, and flavorful, I devoured it on a sandwich bun in about two minutes flat.  If the ribs had had bones, the meat would have fallen off of them--as it were, it fell apart as I ate it.  The chicken was also excellent--very tender, savory, and smoky (be sure to eat the skin--it's the best part!)  Honestly, it's extremely hard to choose between them, but if someone put a gun to my head and ordered me to pick one, I suppose I'd choose the pulled pork--it was heaven on a bun!

The sides were just as awesome as the meat.  The macaroni was very unique in that it had a smoky flavor, and though it had dried out a bit, there were still plenty of places where it was moist and creamy.  The sweet potatoes were delectable, and were very sweet with hints of savoriness from butter and smoke.  If I had to do this order again, about the only thing I'd change is that I'd get half portions of each side so that I could get more of them, since I'd love to try the collard greens and potato salad.  About the only thing that was conspicuously missing was cornbread, which is a BBQ staple, and has been present at every other rib joint I've been to.  Russell, if you're reading this, make some cornbread and start selling it, and I'll be back in a jiffy (get it? haha! :-) ).

Even after washing my hands, my fingers still smell of smokiness and sauce, which is making me hungry again, despite having gorged myself half an hour ago. Never fear, however--we'll finish off the rest of the food tomorrow night for dinner, so I only have to wait 24 hours to indulge anew!  The rest of the family loved it, as well, and I'm sure my dad will be back soon, despite saying he's glad it's not closer or else he'd gain some serious weight!  If you're in DE and are craving BBQ, there's no better place to satiate your craving than Russell's, so head on over--just be sure to get there early or call ahead to ensure he hasn't run out of your favorite BBQ meat and sides!

text:
So literally two days after I wrote my review, I came back to Punchbowl Social .  Unfortunately, I did not have a good experience. So much so that we have to call  the Manager, Hank. I am going consider this as an isolated incident so it won't count against them star wise. However I still feel inclined to tell my story because I hope that management would reconsider their night service practices.

On this particular night my issue was mainly with the night menu. Now I already told you in the first review that the tacos are everything. I usually order beer with my tacos and that's what I chose to do again this time. However those around me decided to buy cocktails or drinks. One person in my party in particular decided to buy a drink on the rocks (I think Crown Royal) and was charged an additional three to four dollars order it that way ( for the ice...). However is not listed on the menu you whatsoever that you will be up charged for ordering on the rocks period. She was not aware of this charge until after her bill came and the one drink came to $13-15. Now, I don't know about you, but anything more than $10 for a drink on the rocks is a lil unreasonable. 

When we called the manager over, he explained the up charge due to it being later in the late night period....then went on to say having a drink on the rocks require a little more alcohol in the glass. But I explained to him that no matter what he was saying, it was not listed on the night menu that you'll be up charged if you order a drink on the rocks and not doing so was misleading. My guest would not have ordered that drink on the rocks if she knew via the menu that there would be an up charge. He agreed with me, my guest decided to pay her bill, but it didn't sit right with me. I'll be back but know I'm checking my bill closely each time and only ordering beer and tacos.

Food (9.0/10) = Bottom line, this place serves fantastic Cantonese fare.  Been here numerous times during many visits to Philly.  The consistent winner for me is the Peking duck served with pancakes, scallions and plum sauce.  The skin is thin and crispy.  Most of the fat under the skin has been nicely rendered off.  The meat is tender and juicy.  Constructing your flour pancake purses filled with duck meat, thinly slices of scallion and plum sauce is rewarding.  You have the option of the half-duck platter ($20) or the whole-duck platter ($30).  You also have the option of adding a second course to this grand duck feast for a few more dollars. (~$2?).  This second course utilizes the remaining duck meat not served with your panckes, tossed in the wok with green beans.  

Other dishes:
1) Pickled chili steamed flounder fillet (Hunan style) = simply wow! The white fish fillets are flaky and delicate.  The flavor profile is amazing.  There's some heat.  There's some sourness.  They tell you upfront it will take 20 minutes to prepare this dish.  The wait is worth it.
2) Crispy soft tofu with pork & shiitake mushroom in brown sauce = Silky tofu.  Lightly flash fried to create the crispy exterior while maintaining the soft delicate interior.  Then placed in a bowl of a thick savory sauce, married with thin strips of pork and shiitake mushrooms.  Of all dishes mentioned in this review, this one is ordered every time.
3) Eggplant with chicken and salted fish = a great change up to those who love the popular eggplant dish with garlic sauce.  I think Sang Kee's chefs prepare this dish well, as the chicken is very tender, and you can taste the salted fish.
4) XO Sauce Fish fillet = the least favorite of the mentioned, but still damn good.  For those of who don't know, XO sauce is sort of like the ultimate sauce created with dried scallops, shallots, dried oysters, etc.  Google "XO sauce" for more details.  The only problem I had with this dish recently was that it was a little too salty.  But it is a minor mistake given the excellence of Sang Kee's other dishes.

As for their BBQ meats you see hanging behind the front window of the restaurant, this stuff is equally good, and you can order the meats by itself, or served as small meal rice plates that cost on average $6-7.  I got two roasted pork + Chinese broccoli on rice platters to go before leaving town recently. 

Ambiance (7.5/10) = Typical Chinese BBQ type restaurant.  Roast pork, duck, chicken and other variety of meats hang behind the front window of the restaurant.  As you make your way inside, table are situated laterally.  

Service (7.5/10) = Lot of people working in this restaurant.  You can easily get a waiter if you need one immediately.  The food is prepared quickly, and comes out hot.  This of course is to be expected with wok cooking.

Overall opinion = Having tried multiple restaurants in Philly's Chinatown, Sang Kee Peking Duck House is the best.  The dishes from the "specials" menu are truly special.  The Peking duck served with pancakes, scallions and plum sauce is definitely a must try if you haven't had it already.  

Of note, this is a cash only place.

This was without a doubt the worst service I've ever had at a restaurant.  I was there with a friend around 1:30 pm on a weekday and we were there for just under TWO HOURS.  

It took a few minutes to get seated, but at least someone (I'm assuming the owner?) greeted us.  Once we were seated it took at least 20 minutes for the waitress to come over to take our order.  And it wasn't busy at all-our waitress was just way too busy taking shots with her friend and hanging out. 

It took around 30 minutes for our food to come out, but instead of giving it to us, the food runner gave it to the table next to ours.  We thought it was our food but the people at the other table started eating it so we figured ours was coming soon.  Nope!  A different waitress went over to them, told them it wasn't their food, took it away and gave them their correct order, all the while saying NOTHING to us.  No apology, no explanation.

We waited and waited, and finally a different food runner brought out our food.  AGAIN TO THE TABLE NEXT TO US.  At this point they had already finished their correct order.  I told her it was our food and she brought it over to us. Again, no apology at all-she just said the waitress had written down the wrong table number.  (I guess after 4 shots in 20 minutes it's hard to remember which table is which.)

The food was decent but the service was ridiculously awful.  We each left a dollar tip and I wish I had left nothing.  I will never go here again.

I had ordered a wedding cake with this company back in 2009. They had worked out a cake agreement with Orange Blossom Catering, in which the cake would be included in the price of our catering.  Well we went in for a tasting, picked everything out.  We had a full catered wedding for 90 guests. About three days before the wedding they contacted us and said if we didn't come down there with CASH we wouldn't get our wedding cake! We were shocked, but figured we would work it out with the caterer after the fact. When we got down there we started going over the details of the size of the cake.  The cake that they were preparing to prepare for us wouldn't have fed 45 people! It was so small, I think the bottom layer was only about a 9" diameter, but I can't remember exactly as this was years ago.

Anyway, we ended up going to Publix because we couldn't stand to do business with a disreputable company that had tried to put us through the ringer and drag us over the coals only days before out wedding.  Thankfully, Publix saved the day and prepared an appropriate sized cake for the same pride that this sham of a cake shop was going to do one that was way to small! Thank you Publix for saving the day and being reputable.  Shame to Cakes By Carolyn!

My first time to Vintage Wine bar was during restaurant week and it was a really fun time. The place is beautiful,  the massive chandelier is gorgeous,  all the dark wood,  it's a really great place to grab a bite to eat and drink. 

Because we couldn't decide we each went with a wine fight,  I did white,  Missy went with sparkling. No way was I passing up duck rillette,  it was delicious, and loved the grilled bread with it. Very flavorful. The escargot in a herbed cream sauce was tasty but a bit heavy for me.  The veggie risotto was calling my name and it was good but the main flavor coming out was red pepper. The rice was cooked perfectly though. It was a nice & hearty dish. And finally,  bread pudding. Had a crispy outside,  fluffy soft center. Two thumbs up on dessert. 

Fantastic wine,  fun menu and at a great location,  I'll definitely head back for a happy hour.

Gotta say, I wasn't overly impressed with this place.  I was expecting more of a "fun" atmosphere considering the name.  Maybe I just a different sense of humor.  It was surprisingly elegant looking inside for what it was...meatballs.  Obviously you get your order very quickly because they just have to pick your ball, put your sauce on it, and that's it.  I feel like you're kind of forced to buy the 4 baller item if you want any different meatballs.  I don't eat that much these days and only wanted 2-3, but if you buy just 2 you have to get the same flavor/sauce.  I feel like you should be able to mix and match no matter the quantity.  
We were seated immediately.  But I have to say I really didn't enjoy our waiter.  He stood over my back and bent over me to touch my menu, while I was holding it.  It just really made me uncomfortable.  After we received our meal, he never came back around to check on us or refill our drinks. 
I wasn't overly impressed with the meatballs, I thought they'd be really large and they weren't.  We were suggested to get the brussel sprouts.  They are the same way I make them at home.  The waiter said all the sides are for sharing with 2 people.  But when we got the brussel sprouts it was just in a small bowl.  It was about the size of a helping I would give myself at home, but it was meant for 2 people.  And because the sides are a la carte, you can quickly add up your bill if you keep adding sides.  We opted for just the 1 side.  The sprouts were flavorless and needed salt and such.  

I'm not sure if i'll be going back to this.  I can just get meatballs at a local Italian place, and honestly the meatballs and sauces I tried that were outside the traditional Italian meatball, just didn't taste right together.  The fajita one was particularly unenjoyable.  

I was excited to try this place for months and was so glad a place opened in Carmel.  But the prices are just a little too high for the smaller sizes of meatballs they are and I just didn't enjoy the staff and overall stuffiness of the place.  I was hoping it would have more of an edgy vibe.

Hands down the best Po Boys. I know many will want to fight me for saying this but I don't care, cash me ousside. I love coming to Bear's on a Sunday. There's really no reason in particular, I just think its just a great place to have lunch on a Sunday. My fiance and I always order the same thing: Cheese fries with bacon, and a large fried chicken Po Boy, dressed, with pepper jack cheese, bacon, and fried jalapenos. With this delightful goodness, I assure, YOU CANNOT GO WRONG! HOLY $#!*, ya'll. Sooooo freaking good. I'm sitting here trying to find the words to describe the amazingness that is this place and I can't. The homemade ranch that comes with the fries is so good you'll want to slurp it with a straw (too much? sorry not sorry). The portions at Bear's are definitely large enough to share. Even a regular Po Boy is enough for 2 people. I hear the roast beef Po Boys are to die for, and while I am not a fan of roast beef, I believe it. 

Oh, and the waitresses are always very attentive and kind. They aren't overbearing or neglectful. The service alone gets five stars from me. 

See ya'll next Sunday!

Came here for a date night while visiting Santa Barbara with the boyfriend. The atmosphere was very romantic and still comfortable. The prices are on the higher end, but so is the food! I would definitely return to this location if/when we are in the city again. 

Bf says the OC location is just as good! Just an FYI.

Okay, there are a few things you need to know about this place. First, it's in a small house a little outside of Downtown Franklin. The parking is across the street. It's very cramped. There might've been 18 tables including the large outdoor section that was on the front lawn.

They sat at a table so close to the front door it was laughable. We practically became the nonexistent hostess stand. The room we were in was cramped with 5 tables. We were very close to everyone in the room. The employees were odd. All of them were dressed like dirty hipsters. A few of the boys seemed super spaced out and the girls were just snappy.  

The prices are high. Appetizers are about $12, pasta is about $30, meats are $30 and up. The dessert was $8. 

We declined an appetizer. The provided bread was bad. Like just unenjoyable. 

You can bring your own wine but they'll charge you $10. The tap water was bad. 

I got a scallop pasta. It was delicious. Four large scallops in a creamy tomato sauce. I give this 5 stars. My boyfriends chicken wasn't so good. The chicken was just average. 

For dessert we got this cute butterscotch pudding with salted caramel toppings. It was good! 

This place has some good qualities but I would be cautious with your time and money!

Yes! Mount Juliet is slowly, but surely joining the rest of Nashville and starting to get non-chain coffee shops and restaurants.

Just Love was one of the first coffee shops I'd tried when I first moved to Nashville and it's still holds up. I went with the cold brew with hemp milk and the "Womelette".  A womelette isn't a waffle at all. Just eggs and omelet toppings cooked in a waffle iron. My womelette had, sausage, cheddar cheese, onions, peppers, tomatoes, and tater tots. Can I say yumm?! Crunchy, eggy, and cheesy. This was delicious! 

They have a drive-thru and offer dine-In seating as well. The staff here is super friendly and I'm stoked to have Just Love in the neighborhood!

Why do people like this place?

Ambiance:  During the winter the temporary walls are put up to protect customers from the cold, but during the summer the tables and the waiting area are all open.  You get in line and take a look at the menu on the wall, which ridiculously has NO prices listed.  It is difficult to get a table, and when you do get one they are all dirty.  There is no one coming through and wiping off tables nor refilling anything at the condiments and napkins area.  The containers for pickled peppers were filled with discarded straw wrappers and there were sticky food smears everywhere.  

Service:  There isn't much interaction to gauge this on.  They take your order and you wait for at least ten minutes for them to call your name.  The frustrating thing is that their loud speaker is pretty terrible and anything that they say through it is nearly indecipherable.  When a fellow dining mate went up to tell them that their ketchup pump was empty, they didn't want to bother refilling it and instead offered him a handful of ketchup packets.  Pretty bad service is you consider the dirtiness of all the tables and the condiments area, makes you a little concerned about what their kitchen is like.

Food:  I never understood why people like the food here, I have been consistently disappointed.  It is not just me that feels this way, fellow diners agree.  The cheesesteak meat and roasted pork is not well seasoned and poor quality.  The chicken for chicken cheesesteaks is not thinly shaved, instead is it in long strips ... poor form.  The backbone of any great cheesesteak is the roll and here they are hard and stale which makes meat and cheese fall out the other end of each bite.  How can you mess up cheese whiz you might ask?  By watering it down ... who does that?!  I don't understand why the fries are always stale and cold because there is always a  long line and wait.  It is like they make a mountain of fries at a time and then spend all day filling orders from that old stuff.  If Mcdonalds can freshly fry them for a dollar and order, why can't this place do it when they are charging way more?!  I couldn't believe it that the last time I went, the soda was flat.  Seriously, every single component of any given meal is a huge disappointment.  When you consider the price that you paid for this subpar food, it is really frustrating.  

Overall:  I have come here five times thinking that the previous experiences must always have been some anomaly and there was something behind the hype, I was wrong.  Don't believe the hype, go somewhere else...anywhere else.

Ordered a dozen oysters on the half shell.  they were sent back.  For one,  they were tasteless 
  and I  eat them frequently.  Plus they were  dry, as if they had been sitting out all day.  But the reason I'm writing this review is the suggested tip.  On a bill totalling 35.28, the suggested tips were as follows:
18% =8.99
20% = 9.99
22% = 10.99

Who calculated this?  Obviously someone who failed math?  the computer?  Nope.  probably an attempt by management to take advantage of those who don't pay attention to detail.   20% of 35 is $7, not $10.  BE CAREFUL!!!

Dined here last night for my mother's birthday and had an excellent experience.  The atmosphere here is very intimate, making it perfect for special occasions. First impressions definitely exceeded my expectations. Upon walking in the door we were greeted by Augusto himself and led to our table where they had placed a couple of red roses knowing from the reservation that it was a birthday dinner. I was very impressed by this lovely personal gesture!

The rest of the evening followed suit.  The service was excellent and our waiter was the best!  Onto the food, I've learned over the years that you can generally gauge the caliber of the food your going to be served by the quality of the bread.  Theirs was uh-mazing! The loaves came out hot to the table, crusty on the outside and warm, fluffy, melt-in-your-mouth, light as air in the center.  Seriously could have made a meal from this.  Started with the crab bisque, which was unlike anything Ive ever had before.  It wasn't heavy and overly creamy like typical bisque, I prefer vegetable based soup and this had just a touch of cream in it.  Also had CHUNKS of crab meat not that shredded crab from a can, absolute perfection!  The appetizers were just as good, again i could have made a meal from the fresh goat cheese ravioli.  At the waiters suggestion, I order the Hawaiian wahloo special with scallops.  It was absolutely cooked to perfection.  The fish was seasoned perfectly, nicely seared on the outside and tender and buttery in the center.  Same thing with the scallops.  I was able to try the crab cakes which were 95% crab meat and the sea bass which was also excellent and came with the best forbidden black rice with huge chunks of lobster.  So freaking good.  They definitely don't skimp on the portion size either. Dessert was Creme Brulee, very creamy and and extra crispy bruleed top!

Everything here exceeded my expectations.  Yes its pricey, but the high quality of both the food and the service is reflected in the price and this place is worth every cent.  Augusto's is creative, unpretentious fine dining with the service and atmosphere to match.  I will definitely be returning here soon!

Drove to Santa Barbara from Los Angeles with a few of my friends and had to make sure we made a stop here! Heard many great things about their fish and sea urchin. The place is located in the Santa Barbara Harbor, so you have to go through toll gate where we collect a ticket and pay later for however long you parked there for. After you find parking, you had to find the place inside somewhere. I expected it to be a pretty big space but it was a pretty small fish market. 

My friends and I ordered the Ahi Poke Salad, Fresh Ahi Tuna, and two Fresh Uni in its shell. The fish were so fresh and I loved how they seasoned the Ahi Poke Salad. A couple of my friends needed some rice with it, but it was perfect for me! It was a couple of my friends and my first time trying uni, so we were stoked to try these "World Famous" Santa Barbara Sea Urchins! Uni is pretty expensive to buy and I never thought I would have the tongue to truly appreciate it until now. Since it was my first time trying uni, my friends made sure that I did not swallow it down in one gulp. To make sure I notice the freshness and uniqueness of it. When I tried it, the uni made me close my eyes and sent me in a different time space! I wasn't too sure what it tasted like, but I loved every moment of trying it. Overall, this place is legit and you guys should definitely check it out!

We try to follow the golden rules of dining with small children: go early, bring entertainment, and be ready to bribe with the promise of dessert. Thankfully, our last visit to B-Line was a great setting in which to implement our family dining operation.  Hitting the counter just after 5 ensured quick service and by hyping the quesadilla the boys were psyched (for the one menu offering my picky eaters would like). 

The staff was extremely friendly (even when we produced a nearly expired Groupon gleaned from a friend) and was nice about checking on ingredients to accommodate our littlest's allergies.  There was another family with a toddler in the upper dining room, so we felt good about taking a seat in there (I do wish there was a slightly larger table for a family of 4 available that isn't bar stool height). 

I had the pan seared salmon salad with avocado dressing--it was nearly perfect. Because it wasn't noted otherwise, I can only assume it was a farmed piece, which isn't my first choice but when the mood for salmon strikes I sometimes i break my Seafood Watch guidelines.  More than a background for the seared filet, the salad was chocked full of deliciousness: mixed greens, cucumbers, snap peas, spinach, sunflower kernels, tomato, red onion, feta and maybe carrots in there too.  The salmon was nicely spiced with just enough heat. The avocado dressing could benefit from some more salt and seasoning. 

My husband had the Italian Sausage & Peppers "sandwich" with a side of herb penne rigate. They did give fair warning that even though the dish carried the name 'sandwich' this was definitely a knife and fork meal.  The baguette upon which the saucy sausage medallions and peppers sat was nicely toasted, buttered and chewy. Pasta was a bit dry, but when mixed with the overflow sauce from the meatballs it was nice.  

The boys each had a perfect plain cheese quesadilla that was made from a locally sourced tortilla and plain jack cheese. Not too greasy, and served with a side of tomatoes, sour cream and salsa.  

Of course no trip to B-line is complete without making a choice from the revolving tower of sugar.  Looking for an allergy safe choice we chose the 4Berry Pie and a slice of peach pie.  Both were wonderful and loaded with fresh fruit (evidenced with a few slightly crisp pieces of peach).  A really nice touch was having a server take our order for dessert without having to wait again in line, that by the time we were ready was 5 parties deep.

One of Indy's must try's. Ambiance is here. Definitely go here if you're having a special occasion or looking to impress. Our reservation was at 845pm. When we arrived we were told they were running behind (no big deal). First round of drinks were on the house for this inconvenience which I thought was super nice. Multiple staff stopped by to check in on us afterward. As soon as we had the amuse-bouche, I knew this place was it. Even the rolls, omg.... (which we were told could be bought from croûte bakery co)

Looking forward to my next time at Vida.

I'm so disappointed in China King. Isn't fried rice supposed to come with veggies as well??  I think all fried rice comes with veggies right?  All I get is onion??  What happened to bean sprouts, snow peas or just peas?  A little carrot?  Geez, I'm going to start making my own Chinese at home. My family ordered other things they were good so this review is only based on the Chicken fried rice which has only chicken, rice, egg and onion. No vegetables for you!!! I guess you need to ask for veggies which would have made this dish so much better. Sigh....Boo, hiss!!!!

The food is OK at best for breakfast but wow does the service SUCK! Some of the people who work here are very friendly and sweet, but there are others who make breakfast here a very frustrating meal. Its basically run by young teens with no manager in site 90% of the time. The majority of the time I went to this location I had some type of problem. I have been overcharged before, Ive been made to wait a ridiculous amount of time for a simple order, sometimes I have to remind workers to make my order/what I ordered, and once in a while I recieve the wrong order. There is a small bar-like counter for patrons to sit but it is way too cramped to do so, so prepare to end up eating breakfast in your car. Once I tried ordering a dozen pumpkin bagels before the season was over, came home and had 8 everything bagels! There needs to be a manager on site full time, and then Maybe this place can turn around.

Went back for lunch - decided to call ahead to try and avoid the fiasco - guy on the phone seemed confused on how to take an order, had me on the phone almost 10 minutes to order a potato soup - waited 15 minutes (figured that gave them enough time to spoon soup into a container) - got there, disorganized mayhem as usual - got in line, waited 10 minutes to even get to the register, I told the girl I called ahead and she looked at me like I was crazy - finally a guy came over and said, oh, yea, I have to ring that up - a tomato and a potato soup right? wrong - they finally  rang me up for a potato soup and put my slip in the back of the line - EVEN THOUGH I CALLED AHEAD - again, an over excessive wait for absolutely no reason - 3 strikes your out, I will not be back

Atmosphere A+, Service A+, the there is the food. This is going to come off as if I do not like the food, but reality is I do like the food. With that disclaimer you may now continue. I am sure they suffer from catering to the Hoosier clientele's taste. This is nuvo americano italiano done well, and maybe the best in Indy. Chris the owner is hands on and that makes a difference. When I want good pasta this is one of the only choices in Indy. The reality is I could not tell if my tortellini were frozen or fresh. If they were frozen they were amazing, if fresh they were good. Price for the food you get may be on the high side, but the upside is that it keeps this place with the right crowd. You want to be happy, this place is consistent on satisfying. The tiramasu is great.

Well I'm glad I got that Groupon deal even if it was just me using it. This place is near as a pin and the staff is friendly. 

Having never been here before, I wasn't sure what to order and since it was a late lunch for me, I got some appetizers. I love war wonton soup and theirs is hot and flavorful.

The potstickers, pork, and Rangoon were all delicious. I would definitely come back here!

Sports bar with an English theme. They have Guinness on tap and it's a typical American electric pump, rather than the hand-pulled you would get in a proper pub. But it *is* Guinness. The TVs weren't tuned to "footie" though.

The meals are English themed, with everything named after a station on the London Underground. Burgers and sandwiches and salads, the usual pub grub plus Scotch eggs, curry, beefsteak with Yorkshire puddings and such.

Service was good and my handsliced potato crisps with cheddar were good with the beer.

But it was when folks started lighting up that I had to pay my tab and head elsewhere. I know it's legal but I don't care for the stink of second hand smoke, so I had dinner and another beer in another place.

Atlantis is one of my favorite places in Reno. Their spa is the best spa I have ever been to.

Plus, I recently chaired a reunion. I worked with the wonderful team at Atlantis & I was able to hold rooms for our weekend reunion plus reserve the ballroom for 200 attendees for dinner and dancing. Dinner was sit down (versus buffet). We started with a roasted beet salad. Our main entree was filet mignon with crab cake and veggies and mash potatoes. And dessert was their amazing cheesecake with our logo. It was simply amazing & many guests said it was the best dinner they ever had. I cannot rave enough about their staff and their hospitality. 

If you're looking for a special event or just wanting to treat yourself please do not miss out on this amazing hotel, spa and casino.

Last night went back to give this place a second chance. I mean it has such great possibilities! Close and it's Italian!!! So we went back and boy was it awesome! We were seated by Paul I believe he was the manager nice guy discussed food and football. Then had Rhea as a server she was so knowledgeable! And from New Orleans' so she has to be awesome! She and my husband discussed beer and what was close to his new fave the Dogfish head 90 minute IPAD and she nailed it he was happy. She gave me a suggestion on the wine and it was great as well. 

     Started with a scallop dish with sun dried tomatoes it was the best scallop ever! Then a tomato and mozzarella salad that we split. My husband is NOT the biggest salad fan and he said he LOVED the salad. They make the mozzarella fresh and you can tell! They need to sell it for it was delectable! For my entree I chose the pork osso bucco that had goat cheese polenta. My husband had chicken Parmesan with bologenese sauce. The pasta was fresh! The osso bucco melted in my mouth as did the polenta too bad I was so full! My husband loved his as well. Kevin was our chef that night and he came out just to make sure we enjoyed it all and we did. He also got my husband to try the cheesecake tres leche and it was good I had to try a bite. 

    Overall one of the best experiences I have ever had! The service was so welcoming and the food spectacular! We will be back!

I thought this was a great place to get pizza in Prospect Park, but sadly, I must say I have no intentions on returning. After my last review on July 18th, I have been to this pizza shop on two more occasions. Both times, the pizza was just bad. I've never had cheese and tomato sauce on cardboard, but I'm pretty sure it would taste like the pizza I had from Cornerstone. 

The very last time I decide to eat here is when I noticed the individual handling money was the same individual running his hands through the cheese, which he then spread on top of the dough. Dude, you're handling money, which is one of the most disgusting things considering how many hands and other parts it has been exposed to. 

What turned me off even more is the young lady working there used her hands to grab a few sticks of celery to include with my order of wings. Cleanliness is a big deal for me and when I witness unclean conditions, consider me a lost customer forever.

The place gets busy and does a great job of turning the tables over and getting people seated.
We tried to call ahead but the system was not letting us in so we walked in in a Saturday night at 7.
We only waited 25 minutes and got a great table with a very good waiter.
The hanger steak was cooked perfectly, the filet was done medium rare.
Fresh steamed vegetables were just that- not soggy or salty.
The waiter was attentive and the service flowed smooth- we did not lose the waiter when it was time for the check.
A very well priced steak dinner.

After, walking in the hot & humid Sun Saturday afternoon June 20th, 2020 I needed to get some food, and cold drink in my system. I decided to go to Bazbeaux on Mass Ave right across the street from The Eagle. You can't dine in the restaurant just yet, but we could dine outside in the shaded area. I had wanted to order two slices of cheese pizza, but I was informed by my server that at the moment they can't offer slices of pizza just yet only small individual box of pizza(10"). The small individual pizza boxes comes with seven slices of pizza. I ordered the small individual cheese pizza along with Coke to drink. When, my order arrived it was so hot, fresh, very cheesy, a tad bit of too much tomato sauce for me, but other than that the pizza was good. For, it to be a small pizza nice size slices of pizza, and I ate all seven slices of pizza at the restaurant. Staff wore their masks, there was hand sanitizer around, when going inside for the restrooms there were plenty of signs on the floor as well as on the wall letting you know where the men's restroom & women's restroom are located. Also, the price wasn't bad small individual pizza(10") that comes with seven slices cost $7.50

I had been here a few times before covid and it was amazing. Everything was fresh and delicious. I just went in there today and ordered 1lb of king crab and it was DISGUSTING. Was frozen, possibly old and horribly over cooked and rubbery. They brought out the bag with almost no butter in it and the shell was soft and bendable. Then the meat was small, filled with water and beyond rubbery. I immediately wanted to puke. The waitress came over and I said this is disgusting before I could tell her what was wrong she just said ok ok I'll get the check. Can I get you anything else? Like what???? I paid $60 for literal trash. DO NOT COME HERE

I order from this place a lot because it's convenient and local. The pasta is a recent addition and it sucks. Chicken and veggies were very dry. Menu says you get garlic knots, but I got sad garlic bread with barely any butter or garlic on it. 

Pizza is decent, sandwiches and cheesesteaks are very good.

Rudeness.  Pure rudeness from the owner.  I wish I could give negatives stars.
My friend and I had just bought a lemon bar (the quality was okay; nothing to die for; it was like Jell-O Brand lemon pudding with thick crust).  We were sitting out front at the one table with two chairs.  I had bought something across the street but was not eating it.
Long story short: the owner came out and confronted us for sitting there.
  
"MAY I HELP YOU?" 
"No, thank you, we're just sitting here."  
"THIS IS FOR CUSTOMERS ONLY!" 
"Yes, we just bought something from here and ate it." 
[Pointing] "THAT BAG'S NOT FROM HERE!"  
"No, it's not, but we were just in the shop and bought something." 
"THIS TABLE IS FOR CUSTOMERS!" 
"Yes, we just bought a lemon bar here."

And then he looked angry and confused.  So we left.
Customer service is important to me.  I would think it would be, too, to a business owner.  I don't care how good someone's food is, I'm not patronizing a shop whose owner is without manners.  And the slice of cake for $6.50 looked dry anyway.
Transphobic establishment, responded to criticism by attacking the critic as opposed to actually fixing the issue.  Supporting them is supporting bigotry.
